issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but the reference implementation and example usage use a three-parameter signature (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and may cause compilation/test failures if they follow the UML/text exactly.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and the code agree. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to describe acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (removing the unused supplier parameter), or (B) modify the template/example and reference solution to add the supplier String parameter to acceptSupplyDelivery and update all calls accordingly. Prefer option (A) if the supplier name is not used anywhere, as it keeps the API minimal and matches existing template/sample usage.
